svg.title: Figure 5. Concentration of the wiring budget
svg.desc: Figure 5. Left: Lorenz curves of the share of wire against the share of connections, longest first, with Gini coefficients all connections 0.40, within the brain 0.34, within the nerve cord 0.33, across the neck 0.15. The longest 1% of connections hold 4.6% of the wire and the longest 10% hold 30.7%. Right: bars of the share of the wire owned by each class of cell type, counting a connection for the class at each end: central brain intrinsic 55.7% at a mean 173 µm, nerve cord intrinsic 32.0% at a mean 211 µm, ascending 22.5% at a mean 363 µm, descending 20.4% at a mean 383 µm, visual projection 5.2% at a mean 157 µm, nerve cord sensory 2.9% at a mean 146 µm, optic lobe intrinsic 2.5% at a mean 134 µm, central brain sensory 1.7% at a mean 118 µm. A power law fitted above 161 µm has exponent 2.99; it beats an exponential but loses to a lognormal and to a truncated power law.
